environment.admissibilityRule: Per RJC-382 owner correction mid-round: a series measured with 1-min load average > 6 at any point is not admissible on its own. Load is recorded at series start AND end below; 'admissible' is true only when both are <= 6.
environment.dockerCommandDisclosure: Every docker/compose command in this lane targeted only manticore29 (docker compose stop manticore29 / docker rm catapulze-job-intelligence-manticore29-1 / docker volume rm catapulze-job-intelligence_manticore29_data / docker compose --profile shadow up -d --wait manticore29, later --no-deps added) or was read-only (docker compose ps, docker ps). The shared 6.3.8 manticore service was never explicitly targeted by name. ROOT CAUSE (found by the RJC-382 owner, corrected from this lane's earlier initial guess that the timing ruled it out -- the owner's timestamp was UTC, this lane's was local, and they in fact line up): manticore29 has depends_on: manticore in docker-compose.yml; this lane's first up command exported inline placeholder env vars that differed from the env manticore(6.3.8) was created with, so compose recreated the dependency (manticore) as a side effect -- no data lost, volume kept. Fixed by adding --no-deps to every up command after diagnosis.
environment.loadPollBeforeCleanRuns: Polled every 30s starting at load 13.36; reached two consecutive checks <=6 (5.32, then 5.22) after ~2 minutes, then proceeded with the clean re-run series.

bulkIndexingThroughput.label: RJC-389 bulk projector path (ManticoreSearchEngine.applyBatch, POST /bulk) vs. the harness's per-document /replace path
bulkIndexingThroughput.method: One-off script (not the benchmarks/search harness) calling applyBatch directly with all 20,000 documents as upsert mutations in one call, against a fresh manticore29 shadow (infix conf as mounted), torn down immediately after. Not gated by the load<=6 admissibility rule (a throughput check, not a latency percentile claim); load was ~7.2 at the time.
bulkIndexingThroughput.comparisonToPerDocPath: ~265x the ~60-80 docs/s measured via the harness's upsertAll (one POST /replace per document, batches of 100 concurrent). RJC-389's 1M-doc backfill design should baseline against this bulk path, not the per-doc figure -- the latter implied an unrealistic ~4hr backfill.
bulkIndexingThroughput.caveat: Real backfill batches are capped at 8MB per request (MANTICORE_BULK_MAX_BYTES) so a 1M-doc real backfill chunks into many bulk calls, not one; this 20k-doc corpus fit in a single call. Real document text (longer/more varied than this synthetic corpus) may also change per-byte throughput.

manticore6_3_8.cleanupMethod: DELETE FROM aanvragen WHERE document_id>='latency-rjc382-' AND document_id<'latency-rjc382.' (range delete on the document_id string attribute; batched per-id deletes via ManticoreSearchEngine.deleteDocument had timed out under load before this range delete was tried). Run twice across this round (once after the contaminated pass, once after the clean re-run), verified back to exactly 505 both times.
